newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan probing TV letter bomb link with 1994 case.
newsitem.headline: Japan probing TV letter bomb link with 1994 case.

text.p: Japanese police said on Thursday they were investigating a possible link between a letter bomb which exploded at a Tokyo television station and a similar case three years ago.
Tokyo police said the writing on the letter and type of gunpowder used in the two bombs were similar, suggesting the same person might be responsible.

The latest bomb addressed to a popular news anchorwoman at Nippon Television network (NTV), exploded on Wednesday at the office of NTV's viewer service department, slightly injuring a network official.
Police said they were probing links with a similar letter bomb which exploded at NTV in December 1994, injuring two network employees. The 1994 letter was addressed to a popular teenage actress.
The gunpowder used in the two bombs was probably obtained from a type of fireworks commonly sold in Japan, investigators said.
The Asahi Shimbun newspaper said NTV received a fax several hours after the blast saying some NTV programs were objectionable and asking the station to cancel them.
Meanwhile, police said a suspected copycat bomber sent an envelope containing firecrackers and a cigarette lighter to another Japanese television station on Thursday.
Police said the envelope was found by a metal detector at the Tokyo Broadcasting Station (TBS). It was marked "Caution: Bomb." A letter in the envelope said "I will kill you. This is no threat."
Tokyo police said they believed the letter to TBS was from a copycat bomber and not the work of the individual responsible for the NTV attacks.
